On evaluation, you had a severely elevated body temperature of 40.2°C, a rapid heart rate, and fast breathing. You were drowsy, speaking incoherently, and had dry skin with muscle stiffness. Your laboratory results revealed elevated liver enzymes and a significantly high muscle enzyme level. Based on these findings, you are diagnosed with heat stroke.

You are a 75-year-old man with a recent femoral fracture for which you underwent surgery 10 days ago, and you have been receiving antibiotics.

You presented with watery diarrhea five to six times per day for the past 3 days that does not decrease even with fasting, as well as decreased urine output. On examination, you had a fever of 38.7°C, a rapid heart rate of 105 beats per minute, and diffuse tenderness across your abdomen. Your laboratory results showed a significantly elevated white blood cell count of 21,190/mm³, elevated blood urea nitrogen and creatinine levels, and a high C-reactive protein level of 342.6 mg/L. Additionally, your stool sample tested positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin B. These findings indicate a Clostridioides difficile infection.

You are a 17-year-old man with no reported comorbidities and no current medications.

You recently had protein detected in your urine during a routine health examination. Your physical examination was normal, showing a blood pressure of 120/75 mmHg, a pulse of 72/min, a respiratory rate of 16/min, a temperature of 36.5°C, and no swelling in your lower legs. Your laboratory tests show normal kidney function with a blood urea nitrogen of 12 mg/dL and creatinine of 0.8 mg/dL. Your first morning urine sample was completely negative for protein, while your afternoon urine sample showed protein, and your 24-hour urine protein was 380 mg.

Based on these findings, your diagnosis is orthostatic proteinuria, which is characterized by protein in the urine only when you are active during the day and is absent in the morning.

You are a 68-year-old man with no reported comorbidities and no current relevant medications.

You were brought to the emergency department after losing consciousness while spraying pesticide in an orchard. Before becoming unconscious, you experienced chest tightness. Upon evaluation, you were found to be confused, with constricted pupils and foam around your mouth. Your vital signs showed a blood pressure of 110/70 mmHg, a slow heart rate of 50 beats per minute, a slow breathing rate of 10 breaths per minute, and a body temperature of 36.4°C. Laboratory tests on your blood showed a pH of 7.30, elevated carbon dioxide levels at 78 mmHg, low oxygen levels at 65 mmHg, and an oxygen saturation of 85%. Other blood tests showed normal kidney function, normal blood sugar, and normal electrolyte levels.

Based on these findings, you are diagnosed with pesticide poisoning.
